title: Compare object contents
summary: toEqual checks values inside objects. This is different from checking whether two names refer to the exact same object.
introduction: toEqual checks values inside objects. This is different from checking whether two names refer to the exact same object. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: toEqual checks values inside objects. This is different from checking whether two names refer to the exact same object.

blocks.code:
import { test, expect, jest, beforeEach } from "@jest/globals";
test("book fields", () => { expect({ title: "Moon" }).toEqual({ title: "Moon" }); });
blocks.title: Compare object contents

blocks.text: The test passes because the title values match.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Use toBe for object identity only when identity is the behaviour you need.
